summary: All four round-1 findings are closed by the changes at 5f4e7167b and the fixes introduce no regression I could identify. PERF-PREP-01: admission_counts(window) in timing.py patches GpuEventManager._trim_gpu_caches with a plain counter keyed on window.phase, calls no clock or CUDA, forwards the original return, and is installed in both modes as the outermost context in runner.py line 95. Because the recorder's framework() hook wraps getattr(cls, attr) after admission_counts has already patched, the profile-mode timer nests around the counter and both are unwound in reverse by their context managers; the native evidence confirms this ordering worked (profile report counts 15/142 equal profile-summary cache_trim_after_pressure calls 15/142, and the raw profile.json contains 157 interval rows plus 2 aggregates). The checkout gpu_events.py still has _trim_gpu_caches called only from the GpuMemoryPressureError retry path (line 935) after _flush_event_pool, so the counter does measure forced pool drains, and the new throughput-1 result (0/0) versus throughput-2 (15/142) resolves the previous inference: the one-stream clean run had no drains, the two-stream runs drain on nearly every callback under the inherited 4 GiB budget. README and timing_contract now state this. PERF-PREP-02: the _ensure_metadata hook bypasses device_call when _metadata_open is False; gpu_task_batch.py seal() sets _metadata_open=False and _stream=None together (lines 161-162), and the original raises its RuntimeError before touching _stream (line 105-106), so the framework error now propagates unchanged; the host test exercises the real framework method on a sealed synthetic context inside the live patch. PERF-PREP-03: runner.py now hashes stage2.fixture, stage2.verify and xtc_fixture, which gpu_accept.py (lines 21-22) and fixture.py (line 15) import, and all three reports and execution-source-hashes.json carry those hashes. PERF-PREP-04: prepare() raises before importing CuPy if kernel or seen is set, matching dense_cube.prepare_profile's contract; device_checks.py and runner.py each call prepare() once. Nine host tests passed in job-43548551.err, four device cases passed, three 1k native cases passed exact per-bank counts with 100/900 windows and 158 callbacks. Evidence is internally consistent across validation-summary.json, copied reports, copy-index.json and artifacts.json. One new low, non-blocking finding: admission_pressure_trims is written to the report only after a successful iteration, so a failed run's report lacks the diagnostic counts; and status.json still records round 1 and the previous implementation SHA.
